newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Extra time for Bangui disarmament - mediator.
newsitem.headline: Extra time for Bangui disarmament - mediator.

text.p: African mediators trying to broker peace in Central African Republic after three army revolts in under a year say they have won general agreement to extend a disarmament deadline following a fresh flare-up.

Mali's former military leader, Amadou Toumani Toure, told Radio France International on Monday that the March 30 deadline had been "relatively short", particularly in the light of bloody clashes the previous weekend.
"Today the deadline is certainly expired," he said, adding that the mediators had had contacts with the appropriate authorities who had shown "much understanding" of the problem.
"I think that we are agreed that we should allow more time and work without haste so that we can find a calm and peaceful solution," he said.
African peacekeepers and army mutineers and their supporters clashed on March 22 and 23. At least five people were killed.

The clashes were the worst since President Ange-Felix Patasse and his rivals agreed an African-mediated peace plan in January. The mutineers, from the southern Yakoma tribe, rejected a Patasse amnesty linked to disarmament, saying they wanted to return to barracks in honour and dignity.
The first mutinies last April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a northern civilian who won 1993 presidential elections.
The latest mutiny, which began on November 15, degenerated into ethnic bloodshed. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order and handed over to peacekeepers.
